version.description:
Auth for Tesla is the fastest way to get a working Tesla API token — and the easiest place to inspect, test, and reuse it. Sign in once with your Tesla account, and your access and refresh tokens are ready to copy into Shortcuts, third-party tools, scripts, or anything else that talks to Tesla's API.

A TOKEN TOOL, NOT A TESLA CLIENT
Auth for Tesla doesn't drive your car, drain your battery, or pretend to be the Tesla app. It does one job extremely well: hand you a valid OAuth token and help you make sure it works.

BOTH TESLA APIS
• Owners API (v3) — the standard token used by most Tesla-compatible apps and Shortcuts.
• Fleet API (v4) — Tesla's modern, officially supported API for developers with a partner account.

MULTIPLE ACCOUNTS
Keep personal, work, and test accounts side by side. Switch between them with one tap, rename them, and add new ones without losing the others.

DEVELOPER TOOLS BUILT IN
• JWT Inspector — paste any token (or pick a stored one) and see the decoded header, payload, scopes, expiry, and a clear valid/expired status. No more flipping to jwt.io.
• Snippet Exporter — generate ready-to-paste cURL, HTTPie, Swift, or Python snippets for the active token, complete with bearer header.
• Test Your Token — run a few read-only diagnostic calls against the Tesla API to confirm your token actually works end to end, plus a local scopes inspection.

TOKEN HEALTH AT A GLANCE
Every profile shows a live countdown to expiry, the time of the last successful refresh, and the detected region (NA, EU, AP, ME, CN) so you always know what you're talking to.

SIRI & SHORTCUTS
All four token actions — Get and Refresh for both Owners and Fleet API — appear automatically in the Shortcuts app and work hands-free with Siri. Build automations that always have a fresh token.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Your Tesla username and password are entered directly in a secure in-app browser — they never pass through this app or any developer-run server. Tokens are stored encrypted in your iCloud Keychain and sync privately across your own devices. No analytics, no tracking, no third-party SDKs.

OPEN SOURCE
Every line of code is publicly available and auditable at github.com/TeslaBuds/AuthAppForTesla.

Disclaimer: This app is not affiliated with or endorsed by Tesla, Inc. Use at your own risk. No guarantee of proper function is given. You are solely responsible for any changes to your vehicle caused by the use of this app.

Made in Denmark.

version.whatsNew:
Auth for Tesla 3.0.2 fixes the most-reported issue from 3.0 and gives the whole app a Liquid Glass refresh.

FIXED — Sign-in survives a password-manager hop
• If you backgrounded the app to grab a password from 1Password / iCloud Keychain / Bitwarden during sign-in, the auth web view used to reload back to the email step, losing whatever you'd typed. Now the same web view stays put when you come back — typed text, current step, scroll position, all intact.
• A misfired tap on Logout / Delete This Account no longer wipes a token instantly — there's a confirmation dialog before the actual delete.

NEW — Token cards
• The Access Token card now shows a live 'Valid for X' countdown badge that flips to red 'Expired' when it lapses, instead of the old greyed-out treatment.
• The Refresh Token card gets a quiet 'Long-lived' badge so you can see at a glance which token is which.
• Tap 'Show token details' for a clean, fully-tabular breakdown of issuer, audiences, scopes, region, locale, and expiry.

DESIGN — Liquid Glass everywhere
• Tools tab reskinned to match the home screen — same glass cards, same TeslaRed accents, same rhythm.
• Toast notifications redesigned as proper Liquid Glass capsules and lifted clear of the floating tab bar.
• Fleet API form fields are now subtle glass capsules instead of the old hard-black rounded rects.
• Consistent spacing and corner radii across every screen via a new shared design-token system.

FIXES
• 'Refresh Fleet API Token' Shortcut now actually refreshes the Fleet token (previously refreshed Owners by mistake when both were signed in).
• App Intents accept an optional Account parameter so a Shortcut can target a specific stored profile.
• Misc accessibility cleanups: bigger hit targets on the account menu, NavigationLink for the Open Source Licenses page.

review.notes:
Auth for Tesla is a token-management utility for developers and power users. It performs OAuth sign-in to Tesla's official endpoints and lets the user copy, inspect, and reuse the resulting tokens — it does not drive vehicles or contact Tesla on the user's behalf.

A real Tesla account is provided for review (it has no vehicles linked):
  Username: noteslavehicles@kimhansen.dk
  Password: cjNZnCfEhfMYHYwn2fyvwkHm

What's new in 3.0.2 (worth verifying)

• Sign-in now survives a hop to a password manager. After tapping 'Sign in with Tesla' and typing your email, you can switch to 1Password / iCloud Keychain / Bitwarden, copy a password, and return — the auth web view will be exactly where you left it, with whatever you'd typed still in place. (Previously the web view reloaded to the email step.)
• Logout / 'Delete This Account' now confirms before wiping the token. A misfired tap no longer instantly destroys the active profile.

What to verify:

1. Launch the app — a brief welcome flow explains what the app does and how privacy works.

2. OWNERS API SIGN-IN — Tap the Owners API tab → Sign in with Tesla. Sign-in happens entirely inside Tesla's own auth.tesla.com web view; the app never sees the password. After sign-in, the home view shows the active profile name, the access token's live 'Valid for X' countdown, the refresh token's 'Long-lived' badge, last refresh time, detected region, and the tokens themselves (tap to copy). Tap 'Show token details' to expand a clean tabular breakdown of issuer, audiences, scopes, etc.

3. PASSWORD-MANAGER HOP — During sign-in, type any text into Tesla's email field, press the Home button to send the app to the background, then re-open the app. Verify the auth web view is still on the email step with your typed text intact.

4. DELETE CONFIRMATION — Sign in, then from the Owners API home tap the account icon → 'Logout' (or 'Delete This Account' if multiple profiles exist). Verify a confirmation dialog appears before the token is removed.

5. TOOLS TAB — Tap the Tools tab to access three diagnostic tools:
   • JWT Inspector — pre-filled with the active token. Decodes header, payload, scopes, expiry, and shows a clear Valid/Expired status badge. The 'Use Stored Token' menu lets you switch between any signed-in token. Also accepts any pasted JWT (e.g. from jwt.io) — no sign-in required to use it.
   • Snippet Exporter — generates ready-to-paste cURL, HTTPie, Swift URLRequest, or Python requests snippets for the active token. Tap Copy to put it on the clipboard.
   • Test Your Token — runs a couple of read-only diagnostic calls against Tesla's Owners or Fleet API (GET /api/1/users/me and /api/1/vehicles) to confirm the token works end to end. Results appear inline. The provided demo account has no vehicles, so the vehicles call will return '0 vehicles' — that is the correct, expected output.

6. MULTIPLE ACCOUNTS — From the Owners API home, tap the account icon → 'Add Another Account' to sign in with a second Tesla account in a fresh profile. Use the same menu to switch between profiles, rename them, or delete one. With more than one profile, the destructive action becomes 'Delete This Account' (it deletes only the active profile and falls through to the next).

7. FLEET API — Tap the Fleet API tab. The Fleet API requires partner credentials (Client ID, Client Secret, Redirect URI) issued by Tesla via dev.tesla.com. The review demo account is an Owners API account only and cannot exercise the Fleet API sign-in path; the screen still renders correctly and the form validates input. Note that the form fields are now subtle glass capsules — that is intentional, not a rendering bug.

8. SIRI & SHORTCUTS — Tap the About tab. It lists four built-in actions (Get / Refresh for both APIs) that appear automatically in Apple's Shortcuts app and work hands-free with Siri. Each intent now accepts an optional Account parameter so a Shortcut can target a specific stored profile.

PRIVACY — The app collects no analytics and contacts no servers run by the developer. Tokens are stored encrypted in the device keychain and synced via the user's own iCloud Keychain. Source code is publicly auditable at github.com/TeslaBuds/AuthAppForTesla.

This app is not affiliated with, endorsed, sponsored, or approved by Tesla, Inc. Tesla is a trademark of Tesla, Inc.
